newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU "regrets" increase in Rushdie bounty.
newsitem.headline: EU "regrets" increase in Rushdie bounty.

text.p: The European Union expressed deep regret on Thursday at an increase in the reward offered by an Iranian foundation for the assassination of British author Salman Rushdie.

In a statement issued by the Dutch presidency, the EU called on Iran to block any move that threatens efforts to reach a solution on the issue of the fatwa, or religious edict, first imposed against Rushdie in 1989.
The Iranian daily newspaper Jomhuri Eslami reported on Wednesday that the 15th Khordad Foundation had raised the bounty to $2.5 million from $2 million.

It offered the reward after Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued the fatwa against Rushdie, imposing a death sentence on him for alleged blasphemy against Islam in his novel "The Satanic Verses".
Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani however distanced his government from the increased award, saying the foundation's decision was unrelated to government policies.
France urged him to go further.

"While noting the position taken by the President of the Iranian Republic, distancing himself from the decision of 15th Khorkad FoundatIon, we urge Iranian authorities to condemn such initiatives," said a Foreign Ministry statement issued in Paris.

Britain has also asked Tehran to condemn the bounty offer, and Germany has expressed its solidarity with Rushdie, "sentenced to death" by Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini for alleged blasphemy against Islam.
In its statement, the EU said: "The European Union deeply regrets the announced increase in the bounty offered to his (Rushdie's) assassins by a private Iranian organisation.

"Following statements made yesterday by President Rafsanjani, the European Union calls on the Iranian government to take appropriate steps against any initiative that might endanger ongoing efforts to reach a solution," it added.
